def process(water2020, water2021, water2022, water2023):
    import pandas as pd

    def prep(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        out = df.copy()
        # Standardize violation to boolean exceedance
        v = out["Violation"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
        out["exceed"] = v.eq("YES")
        # Keep only fresh beaches
        out = out[out["Beach Type Description"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper().eq("FRESH")]
        return out[["Year", "Beach Name", "exceed"]]

    d2020 = prep(water2020)
    d2021 = prep(water2021)
    d2022 = prep(water2022)
    d2023 = prep(water2023)

    allData = pd.concat([d2020, d2021, d2022, d2023], ignore_index=True)

    # Determine beaches measured in all years 2020-2023
    yearsRequired = {2020, 2021, 2022, 2023}
    beachYears = (
        allData.drop_duplicates(["Beach Name", "Year"])
        .groupby("Beach Name")["Year"]
        .apply(lambda s: set(s.tolist()))
        .reset_index(name="yearsPresent")
    )
    eligibleBeaches = beachYears[beachYears["yearsPresent"].apply(lambda s: yearsRequired.issubset(s))][
        "Beach Name"
    ]

    eligible = allData[allData["Beach Name"].isin(eligibleBeaches)]

    # Exceedance rate = mean(exceed) across all samples since 2020
    rates = (
        eligible.groupby("Beach Name")["exceed"]
        .mean()
        .reset_index(name="avgExceedanceRate")
        .sort_values(["avgExceedanceRate", "Beach Name"], ascending=[False, True])
    )

    top = rates.head(1)
    # Return as single-row table with the final beach name for easy extraction
    return top.rename(columns={"Beach Name": "beachName"})[["beachName", "avgExceedanceRate"]]
